docRequirement: settings.md:444-450 binds the sandbox path lists to three prefixes: `/` = absolute (`/tmp/build` stays `/tmp/build`), `~/` = relative to home (`~/.kube` becomes `$HOME/.kube`), and `./` or no prefix = relative to the project root for project settings or to `~/.claude` for user settings (`./output` in `.claude/settings.json` resolves to `<project-root>/output`). settings.md:452 adds that "The older `//path` prefix for absolute paths still works." The rule governs `filesystem.allowWrite`, `filesystem.denyWrite`, `filesystem.denyRead`, `filesystem.allowRead` and `credentials.files`; the page's own examples exercise it — `filesystem.allowRead: ["."]` (:418), `denyRead: ["~/.aws/credentials"]` (:417, :466), `allowWrite: ["/tmp/build", "~/.kube"]` (:415, :465).
current: One validator covers every sandbox path list and it accepts only literal absolute paths. `filesystemRoots` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:303-316) throws `sandbox-<key>-not-absolute` at :312 for any entry `isAbsolute()` rejects, throws `sandbox-<key>-too-broad` at :313, and returns the input array unchanged at :315 — there is no expansion step anywhere in the module (its own doc comment at :293-302 states it is "Deliberately lexical only"). Every path key routes through it: `filesystem.allowRead` via `filesystemSection` (:272, and :277 returns `section` as-is so even a would-be expansion is discarded), and `deniedReadRoots` (:410), `deniedWriteRoots` (:414), `additionalWritableRoots` (:418), tolerant `filesystem.allowRead` (:456) via `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1`; `resolveSandboxSettings` re-validates the same lists at :553, :584, :589, :604, :605. Measured on HEAD with a positive control (bun, importing packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts): `filesystem.allowRead: ['/srv/ok']` resolves to `["/srv/ok"]`, while `['.']`, `['./output']` and `['~/work']` all throw `sandbox-allowRead-not-absolute`; `deniedReadRoots: ['~/.aws/credentials']` throws `sandbox-deniedReadRoots-not-absolute`; `additionalWritableRoots: ['~/.kube']` throws `sandbox-additionalWritableRoots-not-absolute`; `deniedWriteRoots: ['./build']` throws `sandbox-deniedWriteRoots-not-absolute`. Only two tiers feed the parser and neither carries a scope root: the managed floor at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1358-1360 and the user `config.json` layer at packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1293-1303; `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1` (:378-386) has no parameter to receive one, and there is no project-settings tier at all. The `//path` half of the contract already holds by accident: `isAbsolute('//srv/ok')` is true and `dirname('//srv/ok')` is `'//'`, so it passes, and `resolve()` at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:166 (`readAllowRootPair`) and :213 (`denyRootPair`) normalizes it to `/srv/ok` before a backend sees it — but the composed settings keep the literal `//srv/ok` (measured), so `//srv/ok` and `/srv/ok` survive as two distinct entries through `concatDedupe` (sandbox-settings.ts:508-519). The repo already implements the `~/` expansion one subsystem over: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/sandbox-permission-rules.ts:125 does `join(home, literal)` for a home-anchored Read/Edit rule.
divergence: Only prefix expansion is missing; key semantics, merge/floor composition and the `//path` half are correct. Two of the three documented prefixes are refused rather than resolved: a `~/`-prefixed entry throws instead of becoming `$HOME/...`, and a `./`-prefixed or bare entry throws instead of resolving against the declaring scope's root. It is not a wrong value under a right key — the entry never becomes a value at all. The `./`/bare case additionally has nothing to resolve against: no call site passes a scope root, and the managed tier legitimately has none (its policy can arrive over the wire from packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:62), so that arm needs a named refusal rather than an expansion. Note the flat-vs-nested key names (`deniedReadRoots`/`deniedWriteRoots`/`additionalWritableRoots` instead of `filesystem.denyRead`/`denyWrite`/`allowWrite`, and no `credentials.files` key at all) are a SEPARATE divergence — `filesystem.allowWrite` fails one step earlier at sandbox-settings.ts:267 with `invalid sandbox filesystem setting: allowWrite`, never reaching :312.

change.what: Give `filesystemRoots` a third parameter `scope?: { home?: string; root?: string }` and make it EXPAND before it validates, returning the expanded array instead of `value` (:315): entry starting `~/` (or exactly `~`) -> `join(scope.home ?? homedir(), rest)`; entry starting `/` -> `resolve(entry)`, which also normalizes the documented older `//path` form to `/path` so it dedupes with its single-slash twin; anything else (`./x`, `../x`, bare `x`, `.`) -> `join(scope.root, entry)` when `scope.root` is set, else keep a refusal but with a distinct reason `sandbox-<key>-no-scope-root` so the diagnostic says why. Keep both existing refusals AFTER expansion (`!isAbsolute` as the residual guard, and `dirname === entry` too-broad at :313) — `~/` alone and `.` at a filesystem root must still be refused. Default `home` from `homedir()` via an option, mirroring `sandboxRootsFromClaudeRules(rules, { home })` in sandbox-permission-rules.ts:91-94, so the module stays pure and testable. `filesystemSection` must stop discarding the result: :272 currently calls `filesystemRoots(section.allowRead, 'allowRead')` for side effects only and :277 returns `section` unchanged — it must return `{ ...section, allowRead: <expanded> }` and take the same `scope` argument. `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1` takes `scope` in its options object and threads it into :410, :414, :418, :456 and its `filesystemSection` call at :436. Do NOT add a scope to `resolveSandboxSettings` (:542): expansion belongs at the per-tier parse, and its re-validation at :553/:584/:589/:604/:605 then sees already-absolute strings and is idempotent. Update the `filesystemRoots` doc comment at :293-302, which currently states the absolute-only rule as intentional.

Pass the user tier's scope: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1(layer, { scope: { root: CONFIG_DIR } })` at :1298. settings.md:450 anchors bare/`./` user-settings paths at `~/.claude`; our equivalent user-settings directory is `CONFIG_DIR` (packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:21, `~/.nessy-agent` unless overridden). One-line change plus the import.

Pass `{ sink, field: 'sandbox', scope: {} }` — home only, no root. A managed policy has no declaring directory (it can be delivered over the wire, config/managed-delivery.ts:62), which is the same reason sandbox-permission-rules.ts:80-84 skips source-anchored rules with a diagnostic. Effect: `~/`-prefixed managed entries start resolving, and a bare/`./` managed entry is stripped by the tolerant sink with the explicit `sandbox-<key>-no-scope-root` reason instead of the misleading `not-absolute`. One-line change.

change.symbol: 'validates entries the same way as the denied roots' (:63-70) and 'tolerates a bad managed entry and tightens a malformed lock' (:74-90)
change.what: The first test pins the defect: :64-65 asserts `allowRead: ['relative']` throws `sandbox-allowRead-not-absolute`. Under the fix a bare entry with a scope root resolves to `<root>/relative`, so that assertion inverts; keep a throw case for `['/']` (:66-67, `too-broad`) and for the no-scope-root tier, and add positive cases for `~/work` -> `<home>/work`, `./output` -> `<root>/output`, `.` -> `<root>`, and `//srv/ok` -> `/srv/ok` (dedupes with `/srv/ok`). The second test at :82/:86/:88 feeds `'relative'` through the tolerant managed sink and expects it stripped as `sandbox.filesystem.allowRead[1]` — still stripped after the fix (managed has no root), but assert the new reason. Add one negative for `~` alone landing on the too-broad refusal.

blastRadius: Read-path only — nothing writes an expanded value back — but it crosses two boundaries worth calling out. (1) WIRE: the managed floor is parsed from a policy that can be delivered by the gateway (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:62, `MANAGED_DELIVERY_SOURCE`), so managed-tier acceptance/diagnostic text changes for remotely supplied policies — a risk trigger in this repo. (2) PERSISTENCE: the user layer is `sandbox` in `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` (storage.ts:1293-1303); files that are rejected whole today start loading, which changes the enforced policy on an existing install without the user editing anything. Downstream consumers of the composed lists: `resolveHostSandboxSettings` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:57-69) folds the floor, the seeded `credentialDenyRoots` and `sandboxRootsFromClaudeRules` output together; from there the roots reach `readAllowRootPair` / `denyRootPair` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:164, :211), `process-supervisor.ts:148` and `isolation/windows.ts:71`, each of which re-requires absolute — all keep working, since expansion lands upstream of them. Diagnosis surfaces print the entries verbatim and their output text changes from `~/...` to the expanded path: `resolveSandboxReadAllowlist` (sandbox-settings.ts:657), `resolveSandboxFilesystemConsequences` (:753), and the doctor collectors in packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts. Tests that pin current behaviour: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/sandbox-read-allowlist.test.ts:64-69 and :82-88. NOT in the blast radius despite the similar names: the Codex sandbox writer `normalizeRuntimePaths` / `buildCodexConfigToml` (packages/codex-responses-adapter/src/config-writer.ts:162-163, tests at config-writer.test.ts:117-118) has its own `codex-*-not-absolute` refusal and is fed hardcoded absolutes from packages/shared/src/agent/codex-agent.ts:208/:411, never from `ResolvedSandboxSettings`.
userImpact: An administrator or user who copies the sandbox block straight out of settings.md into `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` loses their ENTIRE sandbox configuration, silently. `getUserSandboxSettings` (storage.ts:1297-1302) catches the throw and returns `{}`, discarding the whole `sandbox` key — so a valid `excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots` or `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` sitting beside one `~/.aws/credentials` entry is dropped with it, and the app runs with no sandbox policy while the file on disk says otherwise. The only notice is a `console.error` on the Electron main process's stderr (storage.ts:1238-1240), which a desktop user never sees; it surfaces only if a `/doctor`-class report runs `collectRejectedUserSettingsLayers` (storage.ts:1250+). On the managed tier the tolerant sink is kinder — it strips just the offending entry (`sandbox.filesystem.allowRead[1]`) — but an admin policy written with `~/`-prefixed credential denies then enforces fewer denies than authored, which is a security-relevant under-enforcement rather than a load failure.
notes: Reproduced live on HEAD with a positive control (`/srv/ok` parses; `.`, `./output`, `~/work` throw) before writing this. Files read in full at the cited ranges: sandbox-settings.ts (1-500 via codegraph verbatim, 368-497, 508-563, 560-679 via Read), storage.ts:1230-1303, host-sandbox-settings.ts:1-70, sandbox-permission-rules.ts:80-180, isolation.ts:140-230, managed-policy.ts:1352-1365, sandbox-read-allowlist.test.ts:1-100, and settings.md:390-484 fetched with `curl -sL` (the quoted sentence is at :452, the prefix table at :444-450). Subsystem is `settings`, not `sandbox`: the defect is in the settings-file parser under packages/shared/src/config, while the isolation backend (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts) is correct and its absolute-only re-check should stay. Two things I did not verify by measurement: whether `resolve()` on Windows normalizes a `//path` entry the same way (the settings-layer expansion I propose makes that moot by normalizing at parse time), and the exact rendered doctor text after expansion — I read the collectors' inputs, not their output fixtures. Out of scope here and filed separately: the flat key names (`deniedReadRoots` vs `filesystem.denyRead`, no `filesystem.allowWrite`, no `filesystem.denyWrite`, no `sandbox.credentials` block) — `grep -a` confirms no `credentials.files` settings key exists anywhere in packages/shared, packages/server-core or packages/session-tools-core.
